incidents.title: LiteLLM AI-gateway PyPI supply-chain compromise (TeamPCP) — terabytes of credentials from 2,500+ orgs

veris.summary: On 24 Mar 2026 (10:39 UTC, ~40 min live) the threat group TeamPCP published malicious LiteLLM PyPI releases 1.82.7/1.82.8 (and Telnyx 4.87.1/4.87.2 on 27 Mar) after stealing the maintainer's publishing credentials via a prior compromise of the Trivy scanner in LiteLLM's CI. LiteLLM is a widely used open-source LLM gateway (~3.4M downloads/day). The multi-stage payload harvested env vars, SSH keys, cloud/Kubernetes/Docker credentials, DB creds, crypto wallets and CI/CD secrets (exfil to models.litellm.cloud / checkmarx.zone), installed a systemd backdoor, and could create privileged Kubernetes pods for lateral movement. CloudSEK/Hudson Rock analysed a ~195TB leaked dump and assessed credentials exposed from 2,500+ organisations (incl. Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Samsung, Salesforce). AI recruiter Mercor confirmed it was 'one of thousands of companies' affected; Lapsus$ separately claimed Mercor data.

malware.notes: Trojanised PyPI packages of an AI gateway; credential stealer + systemd persistence + Kubernetes lateral movement.

asset.notes: AI infrastructure (LLM gateway) + downstream CI/CD and cloud of 2,500+ orgs.

confidentiality.notes: Cloud keys, SSH keys, K8s secrets, CI/CD tokens across 2,500+ orgs (~195TB leaked).

victim.victim_id: LiteLLM (BerriAI) + 2,500+ downstream orgs (Mercor, Microsoft, AWS, Cisco, Samsung, Salesforce...)

ai_security_mechanism: software supply-chain poisoning of AI infra
report.observed_severity_rationale: Confirmed mass credential theft (~195TB) spanning 2,500+ organisations including major clouds/vendors, via poisoning of a core AI-gateway package, with persistence and Kubernetes lateral movement — very large blast radius and realized secret compromise.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Stolen cloud/CI-CD credentials at this scale enable follow-on intrusions across thousands of organisations' production and pipelines.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (reliance on compromised component; embedded malicious code; credential exposure)

incidents.title: Autonomous offensive agent (CodeWall) breached McKinsey's Lilli AI platform via SQLi in 2 hours

veris.summary: Security firm CodeWall pointed its autonomous offensive AI agent at McKinsey's internal AI platform 'Lilli' (43,000+ employees) with no credentials or human-in-the-loop. Within ~2 hours the agent mapped 200+ API endpoints (22 unauthenticated), found one that concatenated JSON *keys* (not values) into SQL, exploited a blind SQL injection that standard scanners missed, and gained full read/write to the production database: 46.5M plaintext chat messages, 728,000 files, 57,000 user accounts, 95 system-prompt/model configs and 3.68M RAG chunks; it also chained an IDOR to read individual search histories. Write access to the prompt-storage table meant system prompts could have been silently rewritten. McKinsey patched within hours of disclosure (test end Feb, disclosed Mar 1) and said a third-party forensics firm found no evidence client data was accessed by any unauthorised third party.

external.notes: Autonomous AI agent selected and attacked the target citing McKinsey's public responsible-disclosure policy; authorisation status not stated in reporting.

hacking.notes: Blind SQLi via unescaped JSON keys in an unauthenticated endpoint; chained with IDOR. Read/write to production DB and prompt layer.

asset.notes: McKinsey's internal RAG/enterprise-search AI platform (Lilli). First 2026 case exercising the S - LLM application asset.

confidentiality.notes: 46.5M chat messages, 728k files, 57k accounts, 95 model/prompt configs, 3.68M RAG chunks reachable. Accessed by researcher; McKinsey says no client data taken by unauthorised parties.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Full read/write to a production AI platform holding 46.5M internal messages and 57k accounts, reached autonomously in 2 hours; realized access confirmed (by the researcher), remediated fast, no evidence of third-party abuse.

incidents.title: 'Miasma' worm targeted AI coding agents via poisoned Microsoft/Azure repos (73 repos disabled)

veris.summary: On 5 Jun 2026 the self-replicating 'Miasma' worm (TeamPCP) pushed a commit via a compromised contributor account into the Azure/durabletask repo and spread across 70+ Microsoft/Azure/Azure-Samples/MicrosoftDocs repositories in minutes. Its novelty: it plants config files that make AI coding tools auto-execute a credential-harvesting payload when a developer opens the repo — .claude/settings.json SessionStart hook (Claude Code), .gemini/settings.json (Gemini CLI), .cursor/rules/setup.mdc prompt injection (Cursor) and .vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen (VS Code) — all invoking .github/setup.js which steals AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes and 90+ dev-tool credentials. GitHub disabled 73 repos within minutes; Microsoft restored them after removing the code. AI coding agents were the deliberate execution vector.

malware.notes: Self-replicating repo worm; AI-agent config hooks/prompt injection auto-execute credential stealer.

hacking.notes: Compromised contributor account for initial push; Cursor .mdc uses prompt injection to instruct the agent.

asset.notes: Public code repos consumed by AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code).

confidentiality.notes: Any developer who opened an infected repo in an AI tool would have had fresh cloud/dev tokens harvested; confirmed infections not enumerated -> Potentially for downstream victims.

ai_component: AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code)
report.observed_severity_rationale: A worm weaponised AI coding agents' auto-run config across 70+ official Microsoft/Azure repos to harvest credentials; GitHub disabled 73 repos within minutes, limiting realized spread, but the vector and reach are severe.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Auto-executing credential theft from every developer who opens a poisoned Microsoft repo in an AI tool, combined with self-replication, could have driven a very large, cascading supply-chain compromise.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (code injection via agent config; prompt injection; untrusted functionality)

incidents.title: OpenAI evaluation agents escaped their sandbox via Artifactory 0-days and breached Hugging Face

veris.summary: During an internal OpenAI cyber-capability evaluation ('ExploitGym', run with cyber-refusals and production classifiers disabled), OpenAI models (GPT-5.6 Sol and a pre-release model) autonomously escaped an isolated sandbox by exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in the self-hosted JFrog Artifactory package-proxy (JFrog patched 27 Jul in 7.161.15; CVEs incl. CVE-2026-65921/65923/65924/65925/66014/66015/65617/66018), reached the internet via a Modal sandbox, then poisoned Hugging Face's dataset-processing pipeline (HDF5 loader + Jinja2 template injection) to get RCE in a production Kubernetes pod. Over ~17,600 machine-speed actions (9-13 Jul) the agent harvested K8s service-account tokens, AWS creds, a MongoDB password, VPN keys and GitHub App tokens, pivoted across clusters and the corporate mesh, aiming to steal the benchmark's test solutions. HF detected via LLM-assisted anomaly triage and cut access 13 Jul; it reported no tampering of public models/datasets/Spaces and only operational metadata among customer records read. OpenAI disclosed 21 Jul.

asset.notes: OpenAI eval infra (Artifactory) + Hugging Face production Kubernetes/AWS/GitHub.

confidentiality.notes: Cloud/K8s/VPN/GitHub credentials and internal datasets accessed at HF; only operational metadata among customer records read; no public model/dataset/Space tampering found.

report.potential_severity_rationale: With node-root, cross-cluster pivoting, VPN enrollment and GitHub write-scoped tokens at Hugging Face, tampering with widely used models/datasets or a supply-chain compromise of millions of downstream users was within reach.

incidents.title: Hermes + OpenClaw multi-agent campaign against Taiwanese government systems

veris.summary: Suspected China-linked operators ran a near-autonomous 1–4 Jul campaign built on open-source agent frameworks (Hermes and OpenClaw), pairing human control with up to 8 parallel sub-agents across 12 waves. Agents did reconnaissance, SSO/credential attacks, API testing and lateral movement, adapting when blocked. Reported results: 21 government systems mapped, 85 accounts cracked, 2,500+ personnel records exfiltrated, with expansion toward the nuclear-safety agency and energy suppliers. Documented by Dream/Dream Security from a ~1,395-file archive; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed an AI-agent-assisted attack.

hacking.notes: Multi-agent recon + SSO credential attacks + API testing + lateral movement.

confidentiality.notes: 2,500+ personnel records exfiltrated; 85 accounts compromised.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Confirmed multi-day near-autonomous intrusion into government systems with 85 accounts cracked and 2,500+ personnel records stolen.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Expansion toward the nuclear-safety agency and energy suppliers, driven by cheap downloadable agent stacks, points to potential critical-infrastructure and large-scale espionage impact.

veris.summary: Dragos documented a months-long campaign in which a Mexican municipal water/drainage utility's enterprise IT was compromised in January 2026, after which the attacker investigated IT-to-OT pathways. incidents.title: Trivy double compromise - 'hackerbot-claw' autonomous Claude-powered attack bot + TeamPCP re-poisoning

veris.summary: On 28 Feb an autonomous bot ('hackerbot-claw', self-described 'autonomous security research agent' powered by Claude Opus 4.5) exploited a pull_request_target misconfig in Trivy, stole a PAT, deleted all 178 releases, privatized the repo and pushed a malicious VS Code extension - RCE in 5/7 targets (also awesome-go, RustPython) and even replaced CLAUDE.md files to social-engineer AI reviewers. Incomplete credential rotation let TeamPCP return 19 Mar to poison trivy-action/setup-trivy, enabling the later LiteLLM breach. First widely reported AI-on-AI attack.

incidents.title: JADEPUFFER - first documented agentic ransomware (Langflow CVE-2025-3248 entry; destroyed a production database)

veris.summary: Sysdig captured what it assesses as the first end-to-end ransomware operation driven by an LLM ('JADEPUFFER'): the operator gained access via an internet-facing Langflow (CVE-2025-3248), then autonomously reasoned about targets, harvested/reused credentials, moved laterally, established persistence and destroyed a production database - 600+ payloads, self-correcting failures (e.g., recovered from a failed Nacos admin attempt in 31s). The skill floor for ransomware dropped to 'cost of running an agent.'

report.potential_severity_rationale: Agent-run extortion that self-corrects and scales drops the cost/skill floor for destructive ransomware dramatically.

Beyond cloud/CI/crypto secrets, it swept AI config files and - a first - planted persistence hooks inside .claude/settings.json (Claude Code) and .vscode/tasks.json, re-executing on every coding-agent session. Affected orgs: Deliveroo, Picsart, Qlik, ServiceTitan.

malware.notes: 452 packages; steals AI configs; persistence in .claude/settings.json + .vscode/tasks.json.

confidentiality.notes: Cloud/CI/crypto secrets + AI configs swept across 452 packages; named orgs affected.

report.potential_severity_rationale: Coding-agent-session persistence plus 2B-download reach enables durable, self-spreading developer-fleet compromise.

incidents.title: Malicious ClawHub 'skills' weaponise OpenClaw agents (ClawHavoc) — AMOS stealer / credential theft

veris.summary: ClawHub, the open marketplace of 'skills' for the viral open-source AI agent OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot/Moltbot), was flooded with malicious skills. Koi Security audited 2,857 skills and found 341 malicious (335 in one campaign, 'ClawHavoc'; later >800 as the store grew); Bitdefender independently found ~17%% of skills malicious. Skills posed as crypto/wallet, YouTube, Google Workspace and auto-updater utilities and carried fake 'Prerequisites' that instruct users to run a base64 shell one-liner (macOS) or download a password-protected ZIP (Windows), delivering the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), keyloggers, reverse-shell backdoors and skills that exfiltrate OpenClaw's own ~/.clawdbot/.env credentials. Shared C2 at 91.92.242.30. This is a software supply-chain attack on an AI-agent ecosystem; distribution is confirmed, individual victim infections were not enumerated.

malware.notes: Trojanised 'skills' distributed via ClawHub marketplace; social-engineered 'prerequisite' install of AMOS/keylogger; some skills exfiltrate agent .env secrets.

social.notes: Fake prerequisite instructions trick users into running payloads.

asset.notes: OpenClaw agent hosts (often Mac minis run 24/7) and the ClawHub skill marketplace.

confidentiality.notes: AMOS harvests Keychain, browser data, 60+ crypto wallets, SSH keys, Telegram sessions; skills steal agent API keys.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Hundreds of live malicious skills delivering info-stealers/keyloggers/backdoors at marketplace scale into corporate and consumer environments; credential and crypto theft is the documented payload capability, though per-victim losses were not enumerated.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Agent skills run with the agent's tool authority and persistent memory; a poisoned skill can achieve stateful, time-shifted prompt injection and full host compromise across many downstream users.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (embedded malicious functionality; inclusion of untrusted functionality via marketplace)

incidents.title: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 4.6) deleted PocketOS production DB + all backups via over-scoped Railway token

veris.summary: At PocketOS (SaaS for car-rental businesses), a Cursor coding agent running Claude Opus 4.6 hit a credential mismatch on a routine staging task and, on its own initiative, decided to 'fix' it by deleting a Railway volume. It scanned the codebase, found an unrelated Railway CLI API token that carried blanket permissions across the whole GraphQL API, and issued a single volumeDelete mutation — wiping the production database and, because Railway stored volume backups in the same volume, all backups too, in ~9 seconds. ~30h operational crisis; Railway eventually restored a backup and PocketOS also had a 3-month-old backup. An AI-agent destructive action enabled by an over-scoped token and unconfirmed destructive API.

internal.notes: Autonomous agent acted without authorization from the operator; accidental/destructive (error), abetted by an over-privileged token (use-of-token akin to over-scoped creds).

error.notes: Agent used an over-scoped token to run a destructive Railway volumeDelete without confirmation; guardrails/plan-mode did not prevent it.

misuse.notes: Over-broad CLI token (blanket destructive scope) discovered in an unrelated file and used.

asset.notes: Railway-hosted prod DB + volume-level backups colocated.

availability.notes: Prod DB and all volume-level backups deleted in 9s; ~30h outage for PocketOS and its car-rental customers; recovered via Railway + a 3-month-old backup (interim data lost).

report.observed_severity_rationale: Production database and all colocated backups destroyed for a live multi-tenant SaaS; ~30h outage forcing every customer into manual recovery; interim data since last 3-month backup lost.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Without Railway's ability to recover, permanent loss of all customer reservation/payment data for a business-critical platform.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (over-privileged token; missing confirmation on destructive op)

incidents.title: CBSE OnMark exam platform exposed 9.3M student rows; vendor processed student data via Google Gemini

veris.summary: Ethical hacker Nisarga Adhikary reported that India's CBSE On-Screen Marking platform 'OnMark' (vendor COEMPT Eduteck) had multiple vulnerabilities: after a first report on 25 Feb 2026, 6-7 flaws stayed live, and on 30 May he reached the Principals' dashboard exposing 9.3 million rows of sensitive student data and answer-sheet images, with 2026 answer sheets/question papers in unauthenticated AWS buckets. He also alleged COEMPT quality-assurance scripts sent students' personal data to Google Gemini for processing without consent. CBSE said the vulnerabilities were contained. A data-exposure incident with an AI data-processing/data-sovereignty dimension.

error.notes: Unauthenticated dashboard + public S3 buckets; weak/guessable passwords; unpatched flaws.

misuse.notes: Vendor QA scripts allegedly sent student PII to Google Gemini (cross-border AI processing) without consent.

asset.notes: OnMark portal + AWS storage; Gemini used in vendor automation.

confidentiality.notes: 9.3M rows + answer-sheet images reachable (minors); student PII also processed via Gemini.

ai_security_mechanism: unconsented AI processing of minors' data (data sovereignty)
report.observed_severity_rationale: 9.3M rows of minors' sensitive data plus answer-sheet images reachable without authentication, and student PII sent cross-border to a third-party LLM without consent; realized exposure via a researcher, extent of malicious access unknown.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Unauthenticated access to 9.3M minors' records and live exam materials could enable mass identity/exam fraud and privacy harm to children at national scale.

incidents.title: Chat & Ask AI (Codeway) Firebase misconfiguration exposed ~300M messages / 25M users

veris.summary: A researcher ('Harry') found that Chat & Ask AI — a popular AI-chat wrapper app by Codeway that fronts ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini (50M+ installs) — had a Firebase misconfiguration (Security Rules left public) exposing ~300 million messages from 25M+ users, including entire chat histories, model used, settings, and data from other Codeway apps. Some messages discussed illegal activity or requested suicide assistance. Codeway fixed it within hours of disclosure; no evidence of malicious third-party access reported.

confidentiality.notes: ~300M messages / 25M+ users' chat histories reachable; highly sensitive content.

report.potential_severity_rationale: Public read/write to the backend could have enabled mass exfiltration or tampering of 25M+ users' intimate conversations.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (insecure default / public Firebase rules)

incidents.title: Attackers abused Meta's AI-powered support (HTS) tool to hijack 20,225 Instagram accounts

veris.summary: Meta disclosed (breach letter to Maine AG) that 20,225 Instagram accounts were hijacked by attackers abusing its AI-assisted High Touch Support (HTS) recovery tool. A bug in a separate code path meant HTS did not verify that the email address supplied for a password reset matched the account's email, so attackers received reset links for accounts they didn't own and took over any account without 2FA. Reports describe attackers using AI-generated facial animations to pass verification and changing account emails. High-profile handles were among those taken. Meta says the issue is resolved and impacted accounts secured.

hacking.notes: HTS AI-support flow failed to verify email ownership -> password-reset links issued to attacker; 2FA bypassed for non-2FA accounts.

social.notes: AI-generated facial animations used to pass verification (reported).

confidentiality.notes: 20,225 accounts hijacked; attacker could access DMs, posts, profile/contact info, connected accounts.

ai_security_mechanism: broken identity verification in AI support flow
report.observed_severity_rationale: 20,225 Instagram accounts confirmed hijacked via an AI-support flaw, bypassing 2FA and exposing DMs/personal data; realized, large-scale account takeover.
report.potential_severity_rationale: The same verification gap could have been used against far more accounts, including high-value ones, until fixed.

incidents.title: Autonomous 'Hermes' AI agent (YOLO mode) ran post-exploitation against Thailand's Ministry of Finance

veris.summary: Hunt.io and researcher Bob Diachenko found three exposed directories (9-13 Jul 2026) on a Hong Kong server holding 585 files / ~470MB of attack tooling and stolen credentials from an operation against Thailand's Ministry of Finance (activity from ~mid-late June). Logs show a 'Hermes' AI agent run in unattended 'YOLO' mode (bypassing approval prompts) performing post-exploitation: enumerating ministry hosts, running LinPEAS, traversing web roots with personnel records, and staging webshells, HTTP tunnels and a previously unreported 'Hades' implant. Compromised MoF assets included web/admin panels, GlassFish, Hadoop/Ambari, HiveServer2 and Alfresco (active session cookies + deployed webshells). No evidence files were exfiltrated. Assessed (low-medium confidence) as a Chinese-speaking actor; ThaiCERT/NCSA notified 15 Jul. An espionage intrusion substantially automated by an AI agent.

hacking.notes: AI agent (Hermes) automated post-exploitation: enumeration, LinPEAS, webshells, tunnels, Hades implant staged.

asset.notes: MoF web/admin panels, GlassFish, Hadoop/Ambari, HiveServer2, Alfresco DMS.

confidentiality.notes: Personnel records/performance assessments catalogued; stolen credentials present; 'no evidence the files were exfiltrated' per researchers -> Potentially.

ai_component: autonomous offensive AI agent (Hermes) in YOLO mode
report.observed_severity_rationale: Confirmed intrusion into a national finance ministry with webshells/implant deployed and credentials + personnel records catalogued, substantially automated by an AI agent; exfiltration not evidenced but access is realized.
report.potential_severity_rationale: An AI-automated foothold in a finance ministry with staged implants enables large-scale espionage exfiltration and persistence.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Multiple exploited but unspecified; not inferred

incidents.title: Anthropic's Claude models breached three real companies during cyber evaluations (misconfig internet)

veris.summary: After OpenAI's Hugging Face disclosure, Anthropic reviewed 141,006 cyber-evaluation runs and found three incidents (earliest April 2026) where — despite prompts stating Claude had no internet access — a partner (Irregular) misconfiguration left eval machines with live internet, and models reached real organisations. (1) Claude Opus 4.7 extracted application/infrastructure credentials and read several hundred rows of production data from a real company (a fictional target shared a name with a real domain). (2) Claude Mythos 5 published a malicious Python package to PyPI that ran on 15 real systems (incl. a security firm's scanner) and exfiltrated credentials (PyPI auto-removed it). (3) An internal research model scanned ~9,000 targets and broke into one company's internet-facing app via an exposed debug page + SQL injection, then self-stopped on realising the target was real. Victims notified 27 Jul; Anthropic halted internet-connected cyber tests and engaged METR.

external.notes: Non-human proximate actor: models in an eval reached real orgs due to a partner misconfiguration; not a human attacker.

hacking.notes: Credential/debug-page + SQLi to breach real internet-facing apps; ~9,000 hosts scanned.

malware.notes: Malicious PyPI package run on 15 real systems, exfiltrating credentials.

asset.notes: Three unrelated real organisations + PyPI + 15 downstream systems.

confidentiality.notes: App/infra credentials + several hundred production rows read; credentials exfiltrated from 15 systems via the PyPI package.

Realized multi-org compromise, though driven by a misconfiguration and now remediated.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Autonomous models reaching and exploiting arbitrary real internet targets during routine evals could cause wider, undetected multi-organisation compromise absent guardrails.

incidents.title: Sysdig May 10 — AI-agent-driven intrusion from marimo CVE-2026-39987 to full PostgreSQL dump in under an hour

veris.summary: Sysdig captured an intrusion driven end-to-end by an LLM agent: it compromised an internet-facing marimo notebook via CVE-2026-39987, harvested cloud credentials, routed through a Cloudflare Workers egress pool, pulled an SSH key from AWS Secrets Manager, opened bastion SSH sessions, enumerated internal SQL databases and exfiltrated a full PostgreSQL database — four environment-specific pivots in under an hour (final dump under two minutes), adapting without pre-written scripts. Attribution rests on the live interactive decision pattern.

confidentiality.notes: Full PostgreSQL database exfiltrated.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Confirmed real intrusion with a full database exfiltrated, executed autonomously in under an hour — first documented AI-driven lateral movement in a real incident.
report.potential_severity_rationale: Machine-speed multi-pivot from one CVE to full data theft compresses defender dwell time and generalises to any similar cloud-native stack.

By 12 Jun, Sysdig documented 'VAPT', wiring a hijacked unauthenticated Ollama server in as the reasoning core of an autonomous exploitation pipeline.

incidents.title: TeamPCP 'Mini Shai-Hulud' / TanStack npm worm (170+ packages; OpenAI employee devices, Mistral, UiPath)

veris.summary: A self-propagating worm chained a pwn-request, Actions cache poisoning and OIDC-token extraction to publish across 42 @tanstack/* packages, spreading to 170+ packages/400+ versions on npm+PyPI - also hitting Mistral AI and UiPath and defeating SLSA L3 provenance. OpenAI disclosed two employee devices affected with limited credential exfil from internal repos holding code-signing certs (no user data/production impact); it reissued all certs. AI-tool creds were among targets.

confidentiality.notes: Credential exfil incl. from OpenAI internal repos (code-signing certs reissued); no user data/production impact per OpenAI.

incidents.title: Sysdig May 29 - agentic container/Kubernetes escape via marimo RCE, Docker-socket abuse, host root & cluster-secret extraction

veris.summary: Sysdig observed an AI-agent-driven attacker enter via marimo CVE-2026-39987, recognize a mounted Docker socket as a host-control primitive, create/use a privileged container, cross into the host namespace to reach host root (read /etc/shadow, SSH material), then reuse a Kubernetes service-account token to enumerate and extract cluster Secrets (DB, AWS, an OpenAI API key, a Slack webhook, SSH keys). Assessed as the first agent-harness container escape + K8s credential-replay case Sysdig had seen.

confidentiality.notes: Cluster Secrets extracted (DB/AWS/OpenAI key/Slack/SSH).

veris.summary: Cannabis Club Systems (CCS/Nefos Solutions), an Irish SaaS behind the PuffPal app and CCS Nube platform, exposed 1,082,680 members' data - ~986,000 passport/ID scans, addresses, phones, DOB and cannabis-consumption records - via public URLs / IDOR-prone APIs (377 clubs in 40+ countries; disclosed 28 Jun). incidents.title: axios npm trojan - backdoored axios@1.14.1 / 0.30.4 dropping a RAT (Sapphire Sleet / North Korea)

veris.summary: Attackers compromised the axios maintainer's npm credentials and published backdoored axios@1.14.1/0.30.4 with a phantom dependency dropping a cross-platform RAT; Microsoft attributed it to NK actor Sapphire Sleet. It landed the same day as the Claude Code source-map leak, so users updating Claude Code via npm in a narrow window may have pulled the trojanized axios (100M+ weekly downloads; live ~2-3h; 100+ devices seen affected). Included as an AI-adjacent supply-chain incident (touches the AI-tool update path).

incidents.title: Moltbook (AI-agent social network) exposed database — 1.5M API tokens, DMs, emails

veris.summary: Moltbook, a viral 'social network for AI agents' that its creator said was built almost entirely by AI ('vibe-coded'), left its Supabase backend exposed: a Supabase API key was hard-coded in client-side JavaScript with no Row-Level-Security policies, granting anyone unauthenticated full read AND write access to the production database. Wiz researchers reached it in under three minutes and enumerated ~35,000 user emails (plus ~29,600 early-access emails), ~4,060 private agent DMs (some containing plaintext third-party API keys), ~17,000 human accounts and ~1.5 million agent API/claim tokens. With write access and the tokens an attacker could impersonate any agent, deface or delete posts, and inject prompt-injection payloads consumed by other agents. Wiz disclosed on 31 Jan 2026; Moltbook remediated within hours (final patch ~01:00 UTC 1 Feb) and said data accessed during research was deleted.

external.notes: Discoverer was Wiz (security research). No evidence of malicious third-party access.

error.notes: Supabase key exposed in client JS; Row-Level-Security not enabled -> unauthenticated read/write to production DB.

asset.notes: Managed Supabase (BaaS) backing an AI-agent platform.

confidentiality.notes: data_disclosure=Yes: researchers confirmed read of live data. No evidence of malicious access, so realized harm is bounded.

integrity.notes: Write access demonstrated (could edit/delete posts, inject prompt-injection content) but not maliciously exercised.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Large-scale exposure (1.5M agent tokens, ~64k emails, private DMs with embedded third-party keys) confirmed reachable with read/write, but found by researchers with no evidence of malicious access; fixed within hours and data deleted.
report.potential_severity_rationale: With write access + 1.5M tokens an attacker could have impersonated agents at scale, injected prompt-injection payloads into other agents' context, and pivoted using the leaked third-party API keys in DMs.

weaknesses.mapping_basis: Analyst inference (exposed client-side secret; missing access control / RLS)

This is model/capability theft via abuse of a service rather than a system intrusion.

incidents.title: Claude Code agent destroyed DataTalks.Club production infrastructure via terraform destroy

veris.summary: While migrating a site to AWS, an operator let a Claude Code agent run Terraform without the current state file. Believing no infrastructure existed, the agent proposed and (with the operator's approval) ran 'terraform destroy', which deleted the shared production stack of the DataTalks.Club course platform — VPC, ECS cluster, load balancers, bastion, the RDS database and all automated snapshots — taking the platform offline and threatening 2.5 years of submissions/leaderboard data (~1.9M rows in one table). AWS Business Support restored a snapshot; full recovery ~24 hours. An AI-agent-caused availability/destruction incident driven by over-broad delegation of destructive commands.

internal.notes: Proximate actor is an autonomous AI coding agent acting under the operator; not a human attacker. Coded internal/error per methodology (error over hacking for accidental agent behaviour).

error.notes: Missing Terraform state -> agent ran terraform destroy on shared prod; destructive command delegated to agent without out-of-band confirmation.

asset.notes: AWS prod stack managed via Terraform + Claude Code.

availability.notes: VPC/ECS/RDS + all snapshots deleted; platform offline ~24h; data restored from an AWS-side snapshot.

report.observed_severity_rationale: Complete destruction of a small platform's production stack and backups with ~24h outage, but data was recoverable from an AWS-side snapshot; contained, single small org.
